name: Shift Rewind for a Restaurant Service
note: Every figure is recomputed as of one moment: dragging the service chart (a role=slider with arrow-key stepping) rewinds covers, turns, ticket p50/p90, food, drinks and labour cost from seat, ticket and roster events, and Replay plays the night back at 30 minutes a second on a rAF loop that pauses off screen. The not-yet-happened part is a hatched SVG overlay, labour accrues minute by minute from each rostered shift, and tables, tickets and the Gantt all read the same clock; set --dhs-shift-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Hotel Revenue Board with Iso-RevPAR
note: Because RevPAR = occupancy × ADR, every day is a dot on an occupancy/ADR plane laid over hyperbolic iso-RevPAR curves, so rate-led and volume-led nights that earned the same sit on one line. Segment filters re-stack the daily bars by transitioning SVG y/height and morph the ADR line through the CSS d property, the comp-set rings animate a registered @property angle, and KPIs, calendar, tables and indexes are all summed from one set of per-segment room nights; set --dhs-revpar-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Housekeeping Facade Board
note: The hotel is drawn as its own front elevation in CSS grid — floors as rows, rooms as windows, suites spanning two bays — and the status legend filters it with nothing but :has() rules on hidden checkboxes. Balance reassigns every unstarted room greedily (largest load first, same floor preferred) and the chips FLIP between attendant lanes with WAAPI, while drawer actions walk each room through its real states and all counts, loads and finish times recompute from the same room records; set --dhs-rooms-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Restaurant Group Site League
note: A bump chart of nine restaurants' weekly rank: switching the ranking metric or region morphs every line through the CSS d property (each path keeps one M and eleven C commands so it can interpolate) while rank nodes glide on transform and the league table re-sorts with FLIP. Group KPIs, ranks, the heatmap shading and site cards are all re-derived from the same weekly covers, sales, labour and margin facts, so labour % and score are properly weighted; set --dhs-group-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Guest Reviews and Sentiment
note: Every review carries its own topic phrases with a polarity, and those exact substrings are painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API (prefixed ::highlight() names, ranges pruned from the shared registry on each render, <mark> fallback) without wrapping a single node. Rating, topic and source facets each count against the other filters, the diverging topic bars, weekly trend and KPIs are tallied from the same 30 reviews, and replies post through a validated form while routing uses a keyboard menu inside the card; set --dhs-reviews-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Menu Engineering Matrix with What-If Pricing
note: A Kasavana–Smith matrix on a chalkboard: popularity is menu mix against the 70% rule, profitability is margin against the section’s weighted average, and both thresholds are recomputed from the dishes on every slider input. Dragging a dish’s price or plate cost re-forecasts its covers with a constant-elasticity curve, so the dish, both threshold lines and the quadrant fills slide on CSS transitions (transform and SVG geometry), neighbours that change class pulse, and saved scenarios land in an undoable change log; set --dhs-menu-h to 100dvh in an app.
html:
Brasserie HaldenDinner menu · 4 weeks to 27 Sep

Kasavana–Smith: popular means a menu mix of at least 70% of a fair share (1 ÷ dishes in the section); profitable means a contribution at or above the section’s weighted average.

name: Events and Banqueting Pipeline
note: One list of function enquiries drives three views: a stage board whose weighted totals (value × stage probability) feed a proportional funnel strip, a space diary in CSS grid where clashing holds on the same room and date stack as first and second options, and a monthly forecast of stacked weighted revenue against target. Advancing a lead re-renders the board and FLIPs its card from the old column to the new one with WAAPI, and the diary’s sticky room column gains its shadow from a scroll-driven animation (animation-timeline: scroll(), behind @supports); set --dhs-events-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Supplier Spend Treemap and Price Watch
note: A squarified treemap (Bruls–Huizing–van Wijk) laid out in JS from 104 weeks of per-supplier spend: opening a category grows the supplier level out of the tile you clicked with one WAAPI transform on the layer, and the way back shrinks it into the same rectangle; tiles can be recoloured by change against the prior period with oklab mixing, and hovering sweeps a highlight across each tile by transitioning a registered @property percentage. The price watch, supplier table and invoice three-way match (with credit-note, approval and chase actions) all read the same supplier records; set --dhs-spend-h to 100dvh in an app.
